questions.stem: Per this page, what does the third argument, concurrencyLevel, of the three-argument ConcurrentHashMap constructor do in Java 8 and later?

options.text: It sets how many segments the table is split into, each with its own lock
options.says: The page says the concurrency level determined segment count in Java 7, and since Java 8 no longer controls any internal partitioning.

options.text: It caps how many threads may write to the map at the same moment
options.says: The page says that in Java 8+ the concurrency level only raises the initial capacity to at least that value.

options.text: It raises the table's starting size so that it is at least that value
options.says: The page says since Java 8 the concurrency level only raises the initial capacity to at least that value, as a sizing hint.

questions.stem: Per this page, what happens when a HashMap is created with a load factor of 2.0?

options.text: The map is valid and holds more entries than buckets before it resizes
options.says: The page calls a load factor above 1 valid but unusual: longer collision chains, less memory.

options.text: The constructor throws IllegalArgumentException for a value above 1
options.says: The page gives IllegalArgumentException only for a load factor of zero or less.

options.text: The map treats the value as 1 and resizes once its buckets are full
options.says: The page says the map holds more entries than buckets before resizing, so the value is used as given.
